concepts.title: Road Transport in India
concepts.definition: Roads carry about 85 per cent of passenger and 70 per cent of freight traffic in India, and are classified into national highways, state highways, major district roads and rural roads, with golden quadrilateral super highways linking the four metro cities.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the road share of passenger traffic from 100 gives the share carried by rail, air and water together.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy207.txt road classification and traffic shares (85 per cent passenger, 70 per cent freight)
question_patterns: what share of passenger traffic do roads carry
compute the non-road share of passenger traffic
classify Indian roads by administration

solution_steps.explain: roads carry 85 per cent of passengers
the rest travels by rail, air and water

concepts.title: Railways: Network and Zones
concepts.definition: Indian Railways is the largest public undertaking running the country's biggest network, organised into zones; the dense network of the northern plains contrasts with thin coverage in the Himalaya, desert and north-east, while konkan railway and metro rail extend the system.
concepts.key_idea: Terrain decides the rails: flat plains support dense grids, mountains raise costs and limit lines.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy207.txt railway development, zones and difficulty zones sections
question_patterns: describe the regional pattern of railway density in India
which terrain regions are unsuited to railways and why

state the role of railways in national integration

solution_steps.explain: the northern plains hold the densest network; Himalaya and desert the sparsest
high construction cost and diffused demand keep hills and deserts thin
zonal organisation manages the vast single system

concepts.title: Water, Pipeline and Air Transport
concepts.definition: Inland waterways on the Ganga-Brahmaputra and the west coast canals, five national waterways, crude oil and product pipelines like the Naharkatia-Nunmati-Barauni line, and air services through Air India and private carriers complete India's transport mix.
concepts.key_idea: Waterways move cheap bulk, pipelines move fluids without packaging, and airways serve speed and distance rather than weight.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy207.txt waterways, pipelines and aviation sections
question_patterns: name the national waterways of India

solution_steps.explain: the Ganga, Brahmaputra and west coast canal systems form the national waterways
Naharkatia fields feed Nunmati and Barauni refineries by pipeline
private carriers widened air access beyond the national carrier

concepts.title: Communication Networks in India
concepts.definition: India's communication spans the postal network - among the world's largest with post offices in nearly every village - landline and mobile telephony with millions of village connections, and broadcasting and internet services that link the country's markets and administration.
concepts.key_idea: Postal reach plus mobile telephony gives even remote villages at least one channel to the national network.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy207.txt postal, telecom and internet sections
question_patterns: describe the extent of India's postal network

solution_steps.explain: posts, telephones, broadcasting and internet form the four channels
village post offices and mobile towers extend the network's last mile
communication knits markets, administration and families together

solution_template.explain: 85 per cent of passengers move by road

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is railway density low in the Himalayan and desert regions?

solution_template.explain: mountain terrain needs tunnels and bridges, raising costs

worked_examples.question_pattern: State two advantages of inland waterways for freight.

solution_template.explain: water resistance makes bulk hauling cost far less per tonne-km
rivers are ready-made channels needing little land
fuel savings make rivers ideal for coal, ore and grain
